title: The Primacy of Associations: I Link, Therefore I Think
coreMove: Attach the target idea to a true favorable association already alive in the audience.
sourcePressure: The source says a focal concept can become more important and attractive when linked to favorable meanings already present in the audience.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Any positive vibe near a request will transfer to the request.

hook: An abstract claim that attention changes everything
A generic meeting where someone makes a better pitch
A clever sentence about persuasion before any concrete object appears
counterintuition: You think persuasion happens during the ask, but it happens before it
The obvious factor is not always the important one
Influence is not manipulation when used well
tryThisNow: Set a timer and reflect on attention
Write down three ways to be more persuasive
Ask yourself what matters most right now

exampleSpecs.audience: a charge nurse linking a new checklist to patient dignity
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the checklist borrows meaning from a value nurses already defend
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the nurse places the checklist beside a family photo release form before the shift huddle
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a laminated checklist next to a family photo consent form

exampleSpecs.audience: a vendor linking compost pickup to pride in local soil
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the service feels like waste disposal or care for the market’s own ground
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the vendor weighs a compost pail beside a crate labeled with the farm that will receive it
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a hanging scale with onion skins in a green pail

exampleSpecs.audience: a box-office manager tying renewal to preserving opening night energy
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the subscription links to belonging instead of price
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager places the patron’s old ticket stub beside the renewal form before mentioning the seat hold
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an old ticket stub under the box-office glass

exampleSpecs.audience: an IT lead linking password changes to protecting client trust
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the rule borrows meaning from professional duty already valued
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the lead opens with one redacted client thank-you note before showing the reset screen
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a redacted thank-you note projected over a login prompt

exampleSpecs.audience: a coach linking lane fees to early-morning discipline
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether donations attach to effort already visible to parents
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coach shows the 5:30 a.m. attendance sheet before passing the fundraiser envelope
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a wet attendance sheet clipped to a pool gate

exampleSpecs.audience: a manufacturer linking repair registration to craft pride
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether registration feels like bureaucracy or respect for a tool’s working life
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the maker asks owners to write the first project the tool will touch before the warranty checkbox
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a chisel resting on a blank registration card

skillTargets: link the target to an existing favorable meaning
avoid borrowing an unrelated pleasant mood
identify the audience value that can carry the request
explain how association changes reception without proving truth

tryThisNowSpec: Name the favorable meaning your audience already values, then write how your target idea genuinely connects to it without decoration.
